Vestas Wind Systems A/S Announces Major Expansion to Meet Surging Global Demand

Vestas Wind Systems A/S, Denmark’s flagship wind turbine manufacturer, has unveiled plans for a significant expansion of its production capacity, responding to accelerating global demand for renewable energy solutions. The company confirmed on Monday that it will invest approximately DKK 1.2 billion (EUR 160 million) over the next two years to upgrade and expand its main manufacturing facilities in Aarhus and Ringkøbing.

The investment will fund the addition of new assembly lines, upgraded logistics infrastructure, and expanded research and development capabilities. Vestas expects the move to increase annual turbine output by more than 20% by 2026, positioning the company to capitalize on a robust pipeline of wind energy projects across Europe, North America, and Asia-Pacific.

“Our decision to expand production capacity is a direct response to unprecedented growth in the global wind market,” said Henrik Andersen, CEO of Vestas Wind Systems A/S. “Governments and corporations worldwide are accelerating their transition to renewables, and we are committed to providing the technology and scale required to meet these ambitious targets.”

Industry experts have welcomed the news, noting that Vestas’s expansion reflects broader trends in the energy sector. “This is a strong signal from one of the sector’s heavyweights,” said Mette Rasmussen, senior analyst at the Danish Renewable Industry Association. “With auction volumes and corporate power purchase agreements at record levels, the supply chain is under pressure to deliver. Investments like this help ensure that turbine manufacturers can keep pace with demand.”

The expansion is also set to deliver local economic benefits. Vestas estimates that the project will create up to 400 new jobs in Denmark, spanning roles in engineering, assembly, logistics, and quality assurance. The company has pledged to work closely with local technical colleges and training centers to ensure a skilled workforce is available for the new positions.

Trade union representatives have greeted the announcement positively. “We welcome any move that brings sustainable, high-quality jobs to the region,” said Lars Holm, spokesperson for the Danish Metalworkers Union. “Vestas’s commitment to local hiring and training is particularly encouraging.”

Vestas also emphasized its intent to minimize the environmental footprint of the expansion. The company will invest in energy-efficient manufacturing technologies and plans to source 100% renewable electricity for its expanded facilities.

Construction is slated to begin in the third quarter of 2024, with the first upgraded lines expected to be operational by late 2025. “This expansion will help secure Denmark’s position as a leader in wind energy technology,” Andersen added.
